title: A $47 Billion Company That Rented Desks #shorts
description:
In January twenty nineteen, WeWork was valued at forty-seven billion dollars. Months later its IPO collapsed, and in twenty twenty-three it filed for bankruptcy.
Follow for more fortunes made and lost.
first_comment: Who's to blame for WeWork: the founder, or the investors who handed him billions? 👇

lines.text: Forty-seven billion dollars, for a company that rented desks.
So how did that value disappear?
WeWork leased office space and sublet it, with beer taps and neon lights.
By January twenty nineteen, investors valued it at forty-seven billion dollars.
Then it filed to go public, and showed its books.
It was losing billions of dollars a year.
Investors panicked. The IPO was pulled within weeks.
Its value fell below ten billion.
In twenty twenty-three, WeWork filed for bankruptcy.
Forty-seven billion dollars, built on renting out desks.
Follow for more fortunes made and lost.
